_warning: Evaluation configuration. Deliberately NOT part of config.json. The runtime Config object cannot reach this file, so no inference component can address gold data even by an incorrect config lookup.

protocol.rationale: Paraphrased questions drawn from one conflict family test the same document pair and are not independent observations, so results are macro-averaged by family. The nine reported families are a fixed held-out set scored once. This was called leave-one-family-out cross-validation until 8 August 2026, which was wrong: nothing is trained on the remaining folds, so there is no model being validated and the name implied a resampling procedure the study does not perform. The leave-one-family-out calculation is retained as a sensitivity analysis, showing how far the overall figure moves when any single family is removed, which is the honest use of it at nine families.
protocol.grouping_rule: Every question declares a group_id: the conflict family for a conflict question, the gap topic for an unanswerable one, otherwise the question itself. Aggregation is a mean within groups followed by a mean across groups.
protocol.split_integrity_rule: A group must lie entirely within one split. A paraphrase of a family in the development set may not appear in the test set, because both interrogate the same document pair, the same conflicting figures and the same retrieval behaviour. The leak is invisible in the results, since the question strings differ.
protocol.reporting_rule: Both question-level and family-level figures are reported. Question-level is the plain mean and is included for readability. Inference, standard errors and arm comparisons use the family level. The reported sample is the test split: 68 questions in 32 groups. The 51-group figure describes the whole artefact including development, and is never a sample size for a result. Per-hypothesis denominators are 4 version_supersession families (H1), 5 mutually_exclusive (H2a), 3 stricter_looser (H2b), 3 compatible negative controls (H2c), 5 gap topics (H4) and 17 factual, partial and synthesis groups (RQ1).

enforced_by.split_integrity: sme_assistant.evaluation.question_set.validate_question_set, on both the load and the write path
enforced_by.tuning_boundary: sme_assistant.evaluation.question_set._validate_against_registry; ConflictRegistry.families returns the reported set only, all_families is used for corpus validation
enforced_by.provenance: sme_assistant.evaluation.question_set.check_provenance compares corpus, chunk-set and registry hashes on load and refuses a mismatch or a missing recorded hash
enforced_by.claim_evidence: scripts/build_question_set.py asserts every expected chunk contains its family's anchor text and that figures in required claims appear in the expected evidence
enforced_by.evidence_format: RunWriter.record renders evidence in the arm's own format and raises on an unknown format, so an Arm A record cannot store status markers the model never saw
enforced_by.blinding: write_review_sheet omits the evidence block, which identified Arm A on sight through the absence of status markers
enforced_by.conflict_type_behaviour: ConflictFamily.expected_behaviour derives the behaviour from the type, and question_set._validate_against_registry refuses a question that declares a different one
enforced_by.negative_controls: compatible families must carry a reconciliation and reconciliation_anchors, so the reason they are not conflicts is discoverable in the corpus
enforced_by.retrieval_split: scripts/evaluate_retrieval.py exits on --split test; tests/test_retrieval_evaluation.py asserts it

protocol.tuning_rule: Conflict families carry split: 'reported' or 'tuning'. The eight tuning families are CONF-01, CONF-05, TUNE-01, TUNE-02, TUNE-03, TUNE-04, TUNE-05 and TUNE-06. CONF-01 and CONF-05 were moved there under amendment 1.1 because both were Stage 4 pilot questions. TUNE-03 and TUNE-04 were added under 1.2 so development covers every conflict type. TUNE-05 and TUNE-06 were added under 1.3 because development had only one mutually_exclusive family, whose conflict-pair recall of 0.00 could not be distinguished from a property of the type. A reported family may not appear in the development split and a tuning family may not appear in the test split. The boundary also runs at the level of the fact in both directions: no test question may expect a chunk carrying a tuning family's disputed fact, and no development question may expect a chunk carrying a reported family's.
protocol.preregistration: docs/PREREGISTRATION.md, registered 8 August 2026, amendments 1.1 and 1.2 same date
protocol.question_set: gold/question_set.json holds both splits in one file, built by scripts/build_question_set.py. It is not named test_set because it also contains the development questions, and a name that hides that invites someone to load the wrong half.
protocol.confirmatory_contrast: B versus D. The arms are a tree rooted at B, not a ladder: C to D changes both retrieval mode and verification, so it does not isolate the contribution. C versus D is reported as the practical comparison against the cheap metadata filter and described as such.
protocol.conflict_types: Four types, not two. version_supersession resolves by status filter. mutually_exclusive: no action satisfies both, surface both and escalate. stricter_looser: an action satisfies both but the looser answer is unsafe, so name the stricter figure as the safe course and escalate. compatible: the documents agree and a verifier that flags them is producing a false positive. Reported counts are 4, 5, 3 and 3. Amendment 1.2 of 8 August 2026.
protocol.retrieval_calibration: top_k and min_similarity are calibrated on the development split only, by scripts/evaluate_retrieval.py. Calibrated 8 August 2026: top_k 4 -> 6 (strict recall 0.667 -> 0.815, stricter_looser conflict-pair recall 0.56 -> 0.89, compatible 0.67 -> 1.00, flattening after 6); min_similarity 0.32 -> 0.30 because the answerable and unanswerable score distributions overlap completely and no threshold separates them. Conflict-pair recall is the gating measurement: a verifier cannot resolve a disagreement it was never shown both sides of. The script refuses the test split.
